title: GA4 vs GA4 360: Pricing, Limits and When to Upgrade
description: Google Analytics 4 (free) vs Google Analytics 360 — pricing, event and retention limits, sampling, BigQuery export, SLAs, and when an enterprise contract is worth it.
verdict: Stay on free Google Analytics 4 unless you are hitting exploration sampling, BigQuery export, or API limits — or you need a contractual SLA. Upgrade to Google Analytics 360 only when those enterprise ceilings or support terms are the actual blocker.
quickAnswer: **Free GA4** is enough for most sites: $0, full Google Ads linking, and solid reporting inside standard limits. **GA4 360** is the paid enterprise tier for higher event retention, unsampled explorations at huge volume, larger BigQuery exports, and SLAs. There is no public 360 list price — only a sales contract.
bottomLine: Do not buy 360 to “get better analytics” in the abstract. Buy it when free-tier ceilings or enterprise support requirements are already costing you unsampled analysis, export completeness, or contractual peace of mind. If your problem is privacy, consent banners, or product analytics depth, a different tool beats a 360 upgrade.

faq.question: Is Google Analytics 360 just paid GA4?
faq.answer: Yes. 360 is the enterprise tier of Google Analytics 4. You get the same event-based GA4 product with higher limits, longer exploration retention options, higher BigQuery export ceilings, and a contractual SLA — not a separate measurement model.

faq.question: How much does GA4 360 cost vs free GA4?
faq.answer: Standard GA4 is free. Google Analytics 360 has no published list price; it is a custom annual contract through Google or a Sales Partner. Budget for the contract plus any BigQuery storage and query charges.

faq.question: What free GA4 limits push teams to 360?
faq.answer: Common triggers are exploration sampling above about 10M events per query, the 1M-event daily BigQuery export cap, Data API quota, short event-data retention for explorations (2 or 14 months), and the need for a formal SLA.

faq.question: Does GA4 360 fix privacy or cookie-consent issues?
faq.answer: No. 360 is still Google Analytics with cookies and Google infrastructure. If consent banners or data-processing concerns are the reason you are shopping, compare privacy-first tools or Matomo instead of upgrading to 360.

editorialNotes.title: Pricing and cost
editorialNotes.content:
**Standard Google Analytics 4 is free.** **Google Analytics 360** is a custom-priced annual contract sold through Google or a Google Sales Partner — Google does not publish a list price.

What you are buying with 360 is capacity and support, not a new analytics philosophy. Free GA4 still covers Google Ads linking, Search Console, Looker Studio, and BigQuery export within standard ceilings.

**Hidden costs on both tiers:** consent and legal work in GDPR regions, Tag Manager maintenance, and BigQuery storage/query bills if you export. Those do not disappear when you upgrade.

Use the [pricing calculator](/calculators/pricing/) to compare free GA4 ($0) against paid alternatives at your traffic level, then treat 360 as a quote-only step when free limits force it.

editorialNotes.title: Data limits: events, retention, sampling, BigQuery
editorialNotes.content:
These are the published ceilings that usually decide the upgrade:

| Limit | GA4 (free) | GA4 360 |
|---|---|---|
| Event data retention (explorations) | 2 or 14 months | Up to 50 months |
| Event-scoped custom dimensions | 50 per property | 125 per property |
| Key events | 30 | 50 |
| Audiences | 100 | 400 |
| Explore sampling limit | 10M events per query | 1B events per query |
| BigQuery daily export | 1M events | Billions of events |
| Data API quota | 200,000 tokens/day | 2M tokens/day |

Standard aggregated reports are not controlled by the exploration retention setting. The pain shows up in **Explorations**, **unsampled analysis**, **warehouse export completeness**, and **API-driven reporting**.

If you rarely approach these numbers, free GA4 remains the rational default.

editorialNotes.title: SLAs and support
editorialNotes.content:
Free GA4 has **no service level agreement**. 360 adds enterprise support expectations under a sales contract with Google or a Sales Partner.

That matters when analytics outages or quota failures block paid media ops or board-level reporting. It does not replace tagging QA, consent configuration, or BigQuery cost governance.

If your team’s real need is a named support path and contractual uptime — not higher limits — say that explicitly in procurement; limits and SLAs are sold together as 360, not as à-la-carte free-tier add-ons.

editorialNotes.title: When to upgrade
editorialNotes.content:
Upgrade to **GA4 360** when at least one of these is true:

- Explorations are regularly **sampled** past free thresholds and that skews decisions
- You need more than **1M events/day** in BigQuery export
- You are hitting **Data API** quotas for production reporting
- You need **longer event-level retention** for explorations (toward 50 months)
- Leadership requires a **contractual SLA** for analytics

Stay on **free GA4** when traffic and query volume fit standard limits, you do not need an SLA, and your open questions are about privacy, simplicity, or product analytics — those problems need a different tool, not a 360 contract.
